data.body:
08:0x PDT. GERRIT RECOVERED, and the outage had a root cause worth recording.

The rebar-gerrit host (i-00880b2c7f13527c5) filled its 30-GiB root volume. Diagnosed entirely from the AWS API because there was no shell: the SSM agent read ConnectionLost with last ping 03:09:52. Ruled OUT: hypervisor/network (both EC2 status checks ok throughout), CPU throttling (unlimited burstable, ~440 credits, 0 surplus), kernel wedge (live console, uptime 11.9h, no OOM, no I/O errors). Ruled IN: rebar/host root_disk_used_percent climbing 87 -> 94% and then STOPPING mid-series at 01:33, with GerritReachable stopping at the same timestamp -- the publisher died with the host.

Recovery, shell-free: snapshot snap-06f35ff3a20fe4a73 -> modify-volume 30 -> 60 GiB -> reboot (AL2023 cloud-init growpart expands partition + filesystem at boot). Back at 07:10: HTTP 200, SSM Online, / at 48%.

THE SECOND DEFECT IS THE IMPORTANT ONE. rebar-root-disk-pressure is threshold >85%, EvaluationPeriods=3, TreatMissingData=notBreaching -- and the metric is published BY THE HOST THAT IS RUNNING OUT OF DISK. The disk was breaching at 90-94% but died before 3 breaching periods accumulated, so the alarm never fired; worse, missing-data-is-fine flipped it TO OK at 01:45:10, exactly as the host became unreachable, and it is still green. Only the black-box rebar-gerrit-gate-down probe fired, at 02:05. For a metric published by the failing host, "no data" is the strongest evidence of the condition, and this config reads it as absence of the condition. rebar-gerrit-data-disk-high has the same inversion.

WHY FOUR PRIOR FIXES DID NOT HOLD (measured, not guessed): du gives /var/lib/docker 17G of which overlay2 16G, but docker system df accounts for only ~9.5G with ~1.06G RECLAIMABLE and ZERO dangling images. So ~6.5G is orphaned overlay2 layer state docker does not know it owns -- 67 layer dirs behind 4 images and 4 containers. docker system prune can free ~1.06G against a 29G working set. Every incident in the chain re-tuned the TRIGGER of a reclaim whose CEILING was ~1G. And root has THREE independent accumulators, only one of which prune touches at all: orphaned overlay2 (~6.5G), /var/tmp (3.6G), journald (1.7G).

Filed bug cyclopean-bloodshot-hoatzin (3276-2f81-8c75-4ddd), priority 1, linked relates_to to all six prior tickets: sour-plugugly-rhino, masonic-abeyant-stagbeetle, preodorous-temporary-piglet, scowlful-bovine-dragonfly (still OPEN), beton-naval-eyas, itchy-arbored-peccary. Its ACs demand a bounded CEILING rather than faster reclaim, and a dead-man's-switch alarm. Growing the disk is recorded explicitly as an UNWEDGE, not the fix: the 29 GiB working set is untouched.

STACK STATE: 2503, 2504, 2505 MERGED. 2506 and 2507 are LLM+1/Verified+1 and submittable. 2510 is Verified-1 -- and correctly so: two mechanisms landed in main during the outage (ci_gate .github/workflows/jira-dc-exact-patchset.yml::"Checkout the exact Gerrit patchset SHA", and env_var REBAR_GATE_MIN_FREE_GIB), so our pre-outage baseline reads them as growth; the pytest failures are the same cause via test_the_committed_baseline_matches_the_live_tree. Fix is to regenerate the committed baseline, NOT to add markers for other people's mechanisms. A subagent is doing the rebase/regenerate/push.

Incidentally that new CI gate's step name is "Checkout the exact Gerrit patchset SHA" -- spaces and all. It is exactly the shape that this morning's parse_marker bug could never justify, which is independent confirmation that the fix was load-bearing rather than theoretical.
